We need to generate JUnit 4 test cases for DataUtil class. Steps: list public methods with signatures. Public methods: load(File,String,String) throws IOException; load(InputStream,String,String) throws IOException; load(InputStream,String,String,Parser) throws IOException; readToByteBuffer(InputStream,int) throws IOException; readToByteBuffer(InputStream) throws IOException; readFileToByteBuffer(File) throws IOException; emptyByteBuffer(); getCharsetFromContentType(String); mimeBoundary(); maybe also other public? The class is final, but some methods are package-private (static) like crossStreams, parseInputStream, etc. Only public ones need test. Also internal static methods may be tested via reflection if needed, but we can test them directly as they are package-private (default) within same package; test class can be in same package org.jsoup.helper to access them.

We need basic test cases checking functionality. Edge cases: null inputs, empty streams, unsupported charset, invalid content type, BOM detection, mimeBoundary length and characters, readToByteBuffer with maxSize 0 and negative (should throw IllegalArgumentException via Validate.isTrue). Validate class is from jsoup; we need to include it in classpath. For test, we can simulate InputStream using ByteArrayInputStream. For readFileToByteBuffer, we can create temporary file with known bytes.

For load methods, they depend on Parser.htmlParser() which parses HTML. We can provide simple HTML with meta charset etc.

Edge cases: charset null triggers detection; charset unsupported triggers fallback; content type without charset returns null; content type with unsupported charset returns null.

Test for mimeBoundary length 32 and only allowed chars.

Test for getCharsetFromContentType null, missing charset, weird spaces, quotes.

Test for readToByteBuffer with negative maxSize expecting IllegalArgumentException.

Test for readToByteBuffer ensures bytes read correctly up to maxSize.

Potential BOM detection: create InputStream with UTF-8 BOM bytes then HTML content; ensure charsetName becomes UTF-8 and offset consumed (i.e., content parsed correctly). Since parseInputStream is package-private, we can call it directly from same package test.

We must produce a full Java file DataUtilTest.java with imports, @Test methods, using JUnit 4 (org.junit.Test, org.junit.Assert.*). Use @Before for temporary files.

Add comments.

Wrap file with markers ###Test START## and ###Test END##.

Let's craft code.

We'll need to include parser: Parser.htmlParser() returns a Parser; we can use that.

In tests, after loading Document, we can assert title or element etc.

Edge test for load with specified charset that is unsupported? The method Validate.notEmpty will throw IllegalArgumentException if charsetName empty? It checks notEmpty but not validate charset. So for load with charsetName null it goes detection path; if we pass empty string? NotEmpty will throw IllegalArgumentException. We can test that.

Let's design tests:

public class DataUtilTest {
    // test load(File, null, baseUri) with HTML containing meta charset
    // test load(InputStream, null, ...) with BOM
    // test getCharsetFromContentType various cases
    // test mimeBoundary length and characters
    // test readToByteBuffer with maxSize limit
    // test readToByteBuffer negative maxSize -> IllegalArgumentException
    // test readFileToByteBuffer reads file content correctly
    // test emptyByteBuffer returns capacity 0
    // test detectCharsetFromBom via parseInputStream path? Might be indirect; we can test private method via reflection, but maybe not needed.

We can also test that mimeBoundary returns only allowed chars.

Implementation details: Use temporary file via java.io.File.createTempFile, write bytes, deleteOnExit.

For readToByteBuffer: ByteArrayInputStream with known bytes; call readToByteBuffer(stream, 5) and verify limit.

For readToByteBuffer negative: expect IllegalArgumentException.

For getCharsetFromContentType: cases.

Edge: validateCharset: we can't access directly; but getCharsetFromContentType uses it.

Now write code.

Need to import org.jsoup.nodes.Document, org.jsoup.parser.Parser.

Also need to import java.nio.ByteBuffer.

Test for load(InputStream, null, baseUri) with meta charset: create HTML string "<meta charset=\"ISO-8859-1\"><title>Test</title>" encoded in ISO-8859-1 bytes; call DataUtil.load(new ByteArrayInputStream(bytes), null, "http://example.com/"); then doc.select("title").text() equals "Test". Also doc.outputSettings().charset() should be ISO-8859-1.

Test for load with BOM: create bytes: UTF-8 BOM (0xEF,0xBB,0xBF) + "<title>Bom</title>" ; charset null, baseUri; expects doc title "Bom". Also ensure doc.outputSettings().charset() is "UTF-8". Since BOM detection sets charsetName = "UTF-8". Should be fine.

Test for load with explicit charset param (e.g., "UTF-8") and empty string? Actually Validate.notEmpty will throw IllegalArgumentException if empty; test that.

Test for readFileToByteBuffer: write "hello" to file, read, compare contents.

Test for mimeBoundary: length 32, each char in allowed set.

Edge: getCharsetFromContentType null returns null.

Edge: getCharsetFromContentType with unsupported charset "X-UNSUPPORTED": returns null.

Edge: getCharsetFromContentType with quotes and spaces: "text/html; charset=\"utf-8\" " returns "utf-8".

Edge: readToByteBuffer with maxSize 0 (unlimited) returns full content.

Edge: readToByteBuffer with maxSize less than content length returns truncated buffer.

Edge: readToByteBuffer negative maxSize: IllegalArgumentException.

Now produce final file.

Make sure to include @Test(expected = IllegalArgumentException.class) for negative.

Use Assert.assertEquals, assertArrayEquals, etc.
